item.title: backlog edit has no --remove-step N flag — individual steps cannot be removed
item.intent: Users must be able to remove a specific step by 1-based index via backlog edit <ID> --remove-step N without clearing all steps.
item.description: backlog edit supports --step to append steps and --clear-steps to wipe all steps, but has no way to remove a single step by index. Users who add a step in error or need to prune the list must clear all steps and re-add them manually. The steps array is JSON so jq del() can remove an element by index.
steps: Add --remove-step flag to cmd_backlog_edit() option parser
Validate the argument is a positive integer
After loading the item, use jq to remove the (N-1)th element from steps array (1-based input)
If N is out of range, exit non-zero with clear error: 'step N does not exist (item has M steps)'
Write back atomically using temp file + mv pattern
Add --remove-step to backlog edit usage message
Run shellcheck and confirm zero new warnings
acceptanceCriteria: backlog edit ID --remove-step 2 removes the second step from the item
backlog edit ID --remove-step 99 exits non-zero with a clear error when index is out of range
backlog edit ID --remove-step 0 exits non-zero with a validation error
All other fields on the item are unchanged after removal
shellcheck passes with zero new warnings
